1 --- 2 name: house-style 3 description: The house frontend conventions for this repo, layered on top of the SpartanNG docs. Read before writing or editing any component. Covers BEM markup with Tailwind applied in the component stylesheet, the three-file component, the layout grammar (grid for regions, flex for inline runs, no nested flex faking a grid) and the no-raw-literals rule for hand-written CSS. Where these rules and the spartan docs' examples disagree about where utility classes go, these rules win. 4 --- 5 6 # House frontend conventions 7 8 These are this repo's conventions, layered on top of the SpartanNG docs (the `spartan` skill). They extend the spartan docs where spartan is silent; they never contradict them. Where spartan already has a rule (semantic colors, `class` is for layout only, `gap-*` not `space-*`, `size-*` for equal dimensions), follow the spartan skill; this file adds only what spartan does not cover. One deliberate exception: spartan's examples put Tailwind utilities in the template's `class` attribute. In this repo they never go there; see "Markup is BEM, styling lives in the stylesheet" below. Every other spartan rule stands, including "class is for layout only" on a primitive, which now means the utilities a primitive's BEM class applies must be layout only. 9 10 ## Markup is BEM, styling lives in the stylesheet 11 12 A template says what things are; the stylesheet says how they look. Utility classes in markup turn every template into a wall of `flex items-center gap-3 sm:w-48` that a reader has to decode to find the structure, and they let styling decisions spread across every file that renders the element. So: 13 14 1. **Template classes are BEM names only.** Every token in a `class` attribute, every `[class.x]` binding, and every string inside a `[class]` binding is `block`, `block__element`, `block--modifier` or `block__element--modifier`, lowercase kebab-case. No Tailwind utility appears in a template. That includes `sr-only`: write `class="roster__label"` and `@apply sr-only` it. 15 2. **One block per component, named after the component file.** `hero-card.ts` owns `.hero-card`, `.hero-card__name`, `.hero-card--retired`, and nothing else. A template must not use another component's block, and a stylesheet must not define one. `:host` is allowed. 16 3. **Every component is three files.** `hero-card.ts` with `templateUrl: './hero-card.html'` and `styleUrl: './hero-card.css'`. Never `template:` or `styles:`, however small the component. `ng g component` already produces this shape. 17 4. **Stylesheets are plain `.css` with every BEM class written out in full.** Not `.scss`: Tailwind v4 does not support running behind Sass. The first line is always `@reference "../../styles.css";` (adjust the `../` count to the file's depth under `src/app`), which lets `@apply` resolve the theme's tokens and variants. Write `.roster__row { ... }`, never `.roster { &__row { ... } }`: that is Sass syntax, and native CSS compiles it to a selector that matches nothing, with only a warning. Nesting is fine for states and breakpoints on the same element: `&:hover`, `&::before`, `&[aria-expanded="true"]`, `@media`. 18 5. **App stylesheets are layout only.** Every utility in `@apply` and every plain declaration in a stylesheet under `src/app`, and every class rule in `src/styles.css`, must be layout: display, flex and grid arrangement, gap, sizing, margin, position, overflow and text alignment (the full list is under "The layout list" below). Color, typography, border, radius, shadow, ring, opacity, transitions, cursor, custom properties and anything not on the list are appearance, and appearance lives in `libs/ui`. Padding is allowed in one place: the component's block root (`.roster`, `.roster--compact`, or `:host`), for the region's inset, and only when that element is not a primitive. Semantic tokens only, `gap-*` not `space-*`, grid for regions. Moving appearance onto a wrapper element, or removing a primitive's directive to keep its look, does not make it allowed. 19 6. **No utility classes in TypeScript.** No `cva` variant strings, no `host: { class: '...' }`, no computed class strings. A state that changes appearance is a BEM modifier bound with `[class.block--modifier]`. Never build a class name from data (`roster__row--{{ hero.status }}`): write one modifier per state and bind each with `[class.roster__row--active]`, so every class a template can carry is written out in full. 20 21 Helm directives and their inputs are not classes and stay in the template: `variant`, `size` and the directive itself are the primitive's API. 22 23 ```html 24 25

The theme and the application shell are built, and `ng build` compiles. The unit test passes, lint is clean, and the contrast gate passes all 28 token pairs. I did not run a dev server, and I did not check the responsive or interaction gates, because they need a browser that this stage doesn't have.

**What's in place**
- **Theme:** the spec palette is mapped onto spartan's tokens in `src/styles.css`, with the full `--sidebar*` set. The `.dark` class goes on `<html>`, the choice persists in localStorage, and `prefers-color-scheme` is used until the user chooses.
- **Shell:** `app.ts` / `app.html` hold the `hlm-sidebar` rail with six nav entries, a top bar with breadcrumb, search, notifications, theme toggle and avatar, and the routed region. Shell state lives in a new `app.view-model.ts` (`AppViewModel`), which `App` provides.
- **Routes:** lazy routes for dashboard, roster, `detail/:id`, missions, threats, recruit and settings. Missions, threats, recruit and settings are minimal placeholders.

**Choices you may want to review**
- **Palette deviations, forced by the contrast gate:** white text on amber measured 2.8:1 and white on the destructive red measured 3.9:1, so I used the spec's own dark on-colours (`#241a05`, `#0e1018`) for those foregrounds. The spec gave no foregrounds for success, warning or info, so I chose them to pass.
- **Focus ring:** the spec's amber at 35% alpha is too faint against the light background, and the gate skips alpha values. The light ring is an opaque darker amber (`#a86510`), and the dark ring is opaque amber.
- **`--sidebar-muted`:** this is a custom token, because spartan has no equivalent for the spec's "sidebar muted" role.
- **Route rename:** the roster path is now `roster`, which the slice schematic's own comment expects. The component is still the slice-generator placeholder.

**Not done or not verified**
- Search and notifications are plain controls with no behaviour yet. Later stages should wire them.
- The build reports a bundle-budget warning: 560 kB against a 500 kB budget. It is a warning, not an error.
- `npm run check:wiring` could not run, because `harness/counter/check-wiring.mjs` is missing from this checkout. I checked by reading instead: the ViewModel's public members (`navItems`, `isDark`, `crumbs`, `toggleTheme`) are all referenced by the template.
- The responsive, boot and interaction gates were not run, so the 375px drawer and the 768px and 1280px layouts are unverified.
